# D-640 · 2026-09-06 · Demo — the RELAY IS THE WALL: D-639's first ranked item is **REFUSED** by the board's own RF rule (a SOLE cut against a **zero** mismatch budget), `NOT_A_POCKET` is exposed as an ABSENCE OF MEASUREMENT and deleted, and the whole pour-served family — all 18 lands — is censused for the first time

    authority  f496d2f39c0827248a47ab7d47efa4322f078b68d2da1d91ae6585d97bf8f875
            -> f496d2f39c0827248a47ab7d47efa4322f078b68d2da1d91ae6585d97bf8f875
    NO COPPER MOVED.  Zero tracks, zero vias, zero zones, zero rule areas,
      zero `.kicad_dru` change, zero placement change.  Every screen re-reads
      the board's sha256 after its last trial and reports
      `authoritative_unchanged: true`.
    `hardware/beta-v2` UNTOUCHED (`git status --short hardware/beta-v2/` empty).
    THE TEN STANDING CONTRACTS: **10/10 RAN, 10/10 PASS**
      (`evidence/d640-contract-regression.json`, baseline `d632`).  They differ
      from that baseline in exactly the three fields D-639 already documented
      and in nothing else: `board_sha256`, `In1.Cu` reference-plane area
      9429.543 -> 9425.846 mm2, and `PP2`'s `GND|B` island count 58 -> 57.
      This iteration moved nothing.

D-639 closed with a ranked list whose first item was *"re-take
`screen_segment_evict` on the promoted board and gate `GND U9.16`"*, and called
that land *"measured, planned and ready ... the cheapest closure this board
has"*.  **It must not be gated.**  Re-taking it on the promoted board is the
cheap half; the expensive half is that nobody had asked what the cut COSTS.

## 1. THE CITATION GUARD — distance is not a price

`screen_segment_evict` walks its candidate tracks NEAREST-FIRST and stops at
the FIRST one whose single cut opens a land (its QUESTION 2).  Every instrument
downstream — `relay_price`, `screen_relay_transaction`, `--plan-out`, the gate
— inherits that one choice without ever learning whether there was another, and
without ever learning whose track it is.  **Distance to the land is not a
price.  What a cut costs is what the RELAY costs, and that is decided by whose
track it is.**

New tracked **`screen_cut_choice.py`**.  For a land that opens it enumerates
EVERY candidate, cuts each ALONE, reports every one that opens the barrel site,
and greps the citation each cut net carries in this repository's own contracts
— `checks/*.py`, `verify_promotion.py`, `protected_copper.py` and the board's
`.kicad_dru`.  **The citations are READ, never listed**: a hand-maintained
"sensitive nets" table is a second copy of the truth and would be wrong the day
a rule changed.  A positive control rides along: `screen_segment_evict`'s own
chosen cut must appear in the opener list (`reproduces_evidence_cut`), or the
two instruments disagree about the same land and this one is wrong.  It is
`true` on both lands that open.

Both instruments now measure on ONE lattice: `screen_segment_evict.main`'s
`Field`/rung/`body_landing` construction is lifted out verbatim as
`land_field()` so a second instrument cannot drift from it.  That extraction is
the ONLY change to any existing file in this decision — `git diff --numstat` is
one file, and its behaviour is unchanged except where section 3 says otherwise.

## 2. `GND U9.16` IS REFUSED, NOT READY — and the reason is the board's own rule

**It is a `SOLE_CUT`.**  Of 20 candidate tracks exactly ONE opens the land; the
other **19 all refuse `NO_BODY_VIA_SITE`**.  That one is
`/04_SPI_B_RADIOS_NFC/NFC_RFO2` — the LONGER of the two 13.56 MHz transmit arms
— and it is the most heavily constrained net the screen could have landed on:

    six .kicad_dru rules   NFC transmit arm minimum width - equal both arms
                           NFC transmit arm routed clearance
                           NFC transmit arms are forbidden on In2
                           NFC transmit arms carry no via - a via is an asymmetry
                           NFC transmit arms stay on B.Cu
                           SWITCH_NODE to NFC transmit arms separation
    two NET-level cites    checks/placement_contract.py
                           checks/rf_symmetry_contract.py
    one class cite         checks/plane_return_path.py  (NFC_RF is reference-critical)

**And `RF2`'s budget is ZERO.**  `checks/rf_symmetry_contract.py` run on the
promoted board reports `arm_mismatch_budget_mm: 0.0`,
`arm_mismatch_growth_mm: 0.0`, `arm_mismatch_mm_now: 2.8702`.  D-639's own
accepted relay for this land is **2.6872 -> 3.09974 mm** on the LONGER arm
(`evidence/d639-relay-joint-u916-g25.json`), so the recorded mismatch would go
**2.8702 -> 3.2827 mm, a growth of 0.41254 mm against a budget of zero.**

**The transaction D-639 left "ready" would have been refused by a standing
contract AFTER a full-authority gate run was spent on it.**  That is the third
gate run this family has nearly cost, and it is the one the citation guard
exists to prevent.  `GND U9.16` is now **CLOSED as REFUSED** — not carried, not
open, and not a routing question: closing it means moving an NFC transmit arm,
which is PM-3.

## 3. `NOT_A_POCKET` WAS AN ABSENCE OF MEASUREMENT, AND IT IS DELETED

`screen_segment_evict` ended any land whose UNCUT escape failed for a reason
other than `NO_VIA_SITE`/`NO_BODY_VIA_SITE` — in practice `NO_LEGAL_ESCAPE` —
as `NOT_A_POCKET`, **before offering it a single cut**.  That reads an absence
of measurement as a measurement, and it had been doing so for every land of
this kind since the screen was written.

It is wrong on its own terms.  `Cuts` removes FOREIGN ROUTED COPPER and nothing
else, so it can only **ADD** room; `candidates` needs no escape to build its
list.  An escape that fails on the uncut board can succeed once the copper
beside the pad is gone.  **Seven lands were being skipped.**

The verdict is deleted.  Every land now reaches the cut stage and carries the
reason its uncut escape gave (`uncut_escape`), so a `SEGMENT_WALL` here is a
refusal and no longer a skip.

**RE-RUN, AND THE ANSWER DID NOT MOVE — WHICH IS THE POINT.**  All seven come
back `SEGMENT_WALL` with all 20 candidates cut at once and the escape still
`NO_LEGAL_ESCAPE`.  Nothing was unlocked.  What changed is that seven "never
asked" became seven **measured refusals**.

## 4. AND THE REFUSAL NAMES ITSELF: NOT ONE BLOCKER IS A TRACK

Every blocker `stitch_pad` names in all seven escapes is a **PAD** or the
**BOARD EDGE**:

    +3V3  U4.3   >= 0.400 mm   U4.4 (x54), C6.2 (x7), U4.1 (x6), R119.2 (x3)
    +3V3  U4.5   >= 0.400 mm   U4.6 (x41), U4.4 (x19), C6.2 (x5), C7.2 (x3)
    +3V3  U4.8   >= 0.400 mm   U4.9 (x44), U4.7 (x13), U4.6 (x4), U4.1 (x4)
    +3V3  U5.2   >= 0.400 mm   U5.1 (x56), R15.2 (x10), R15.1 (x3), C10.2 (x3)
    SYS   U12.1  >= 0.500 mm   U12.2 (x69), C24.2 (x2), TP47.1 (x1)
    SYS   U11.1  >= 0.500 mm   U11.2 (x54), R36.1 (x7), R37.2 (x3), C36.2 (x3)
    GND   MK1.4  >= 0.150 mm   MK1.* (x67), board_edge (x5)

In every case the dominant blocker is the land's OWN package's ADJACENT PIN.
**No eviction of any size can move a pad**, and the census now proves that
directly rather than assuming it.  These seven are a PLACEMENT finding (PM-3)
for a named, measured reason.

**THIS QUALIFIES A STANDING INSTRUMENT'S PRESCRIPTION.**
`screen_escape_class.py` classes four of the seven `CLEAR` — *"this package can
launch the contract width; a router refusal here is ROUTED COPPER, not the
land"* — with margins **+0.300 mm (`U12.1`), +0.275 (`U4.8`), +0.200 (`U11.1`),
+0.135 (`MK1.4`)** and a 1.000 mm widest launch
(`evidence/d640-escape-class-pourfamily.json`).  This census then cut every
unprotected foreign TRACK within 8.0 mm of each and the escape still refused.
`CLEAR` is a statement about the widest launch in EXACT GEOMETRY; it does NOT
entail that an eviction will fix the refusal.  What is left in those windows is
foreign VIAS — 46 at `U12.1`, 38 at `U4.8`, 29 at `U11.1`, 4 at `MK1.4` — which
a segment cut may not touch because a barrel is a hole through every layer, and
the pads named above, which nothing may touch.  **`CLEAR` must not be read as
"an eviction will open it".**

## 5. THE POUR-SERVED FAMILY, CENSUSED — ALL 18 LANDS

`evidence/d640-segment-evict-pourfamily.json`, `+3V3` / `BQ25185_SYS` / `GND`,
one run, `--cap 20 --body-landing --relay-own-layer`:

                             at once and the site is still refused
    SEGMENT_OPENS       2    GND U9.16, GND J3.A12/B1     (one cut each)
    SEGMENT_SET_OPENS   2    +3V3 R39.1 (2 cuts), BQ25185_SYS C26.2 (7 cuts)

**Four lands open, and the citation guard ranks them
(`evidence/d640-cut-choice-pourfamily.json`):**

    GND U9.16      SOLE_CUT       NFC_RFO2       6 DRU rules, 2 net cites  REFUSED (section 2)
    GND J3.A12/B1  SOLE_CUT       Net-(J3-CC2)   ZERO rules, ZERO cites    ** UNCITED **
    +3V3 R39.1     NO_SINGLE_CUT  (2-track set)  D-639: relay splits a GND pour
    BQ25185_SYS
        C26.2      NO_SINGLE_CUT  (7-track set)  see section 6

**`Net-(J3-CC2)` IS THE ONLY UNCONSTRAINED CUT ON THIS BOARD.**  Nothing in
this repository — no `checks/*.py`, no `.kicad_dru` rule, no protected-copper
pattern — has a net-level opinion about it.  Read beside section 2 this
INVERTS D-639's ranking: the land it called ready carries the most constrained
cut on the board, and the land it carried as a wall carries the only free one.
D-638 already measured why that land had not moved — `Net-(J3-CC2)` would not
go back *"on a board where NOTHING else changed"*, which D-638 itself named a
`LATTICE_WALL`, **a refusal of the instrument and not of the board**.

**A DEFECT IN THE NEW INSTRUMENT, FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE IT MISLED ANYTHING.**
The first run reported `Net-(J3-CC2)` as CITED — three contract files and two
`.kicad_dru` rules.  Every one of those hits was the literal string `Default`,
its netclass, matched inside a block about something else.  `Default` is this
board's catch-all: the word appears in every `argparse` call in those files, and
a class that constrains nothing may not make a net look constrained.  The class
is now excluded, class-level and net-level citations are reported separately,
and `uncited_openers` means **no contract names this NET**.  Had it not been
caught, the guard would have steered the next iteration AWAY from the best
candidate it found.

## 6. `BQ25185_SYS C26.2` — the closest this board has come, and ONE net refuses it

Never through D-639's joint arm before.  Run at `--grid 25000 --arm joint`
(`evidence/d640-relay-joint-c262-g25.json`), round 1 lays a **0.972 mm** stitch
and gets **TWO of the three cut nets back**:

    /08_BUTTONS_EXPANDERS/BTN_DOWN_N   5.8398 -> 6.5295 mm   ok
    /BQ25185_STAT2                     2.8607 -> 3.5648 mm   ok
    Net-(U12-PS_SYNC)                  2.7036 -> NO_PATH     REFUSES THE LAND

Round 2 finds no second barrel site inside the net's own body pour within
8.0 mm (`NO_BODY_VIA_SITE`), so the arm exhausts after 2 of its 12 tries.
`BQ25185_SYS C26.2` is refused for exactly ONE named reason, on the net with
the most open edges on the board (7).

## 7. THE CORRIDOR FAMILY AGREES, AND NAMES THE SAME WALL

`screen_corridor_detour.py` had never been run board-wide, and never on the
promoted board.  **PARTIAL AND SAID SO** — 4 of 17 nets completed, 1 timed out
at 1500 s, 12 never started
(`evidence/d640-corridor-detour-census.json`, `coverage` states it):

    /01_POWER_TREE/USB_D_CONN_P  J3.A6/B6<->U10.3   DETOURABLE, UNRELAYABLE
                                 48 crossing, minimal 4, lane 9.647 mm
                                 irreducible_nets: ['GND']
                                 relay: /I2S_LRCLK NO_PATH, GND NO_PATH
    /04_SPI_B_RADIOS_NFC/NFC_VDD_RF  <->U9.14       DETOURABLE, UNRELAYABLE
                                 170 crossing, minimal 3 (ALL NFC_RFO2)
                                 irreducible_nets: []   <-- see below
                                 relay: NFC_RFO2 NO_PATH
    /USB_D_MCU_N  R33.2<->U1.13                     SEGMENT_WALL (117 crossing)
    /USB_D_MCU_P  R34.2<->U1.14                     SEGMENT_WALL (158 crossing)
    /ACC_PWR_EN                                     TIMED OUT at 1500 s

`NFC_RFO2` is the wall of a SECOND open edge, by the same nearest-first bias
section 1 is about — and `irreducible_nets: []` **proves a cut set that spares
it exists**, because that clause holds out every crossing track EXCEPT one
net's and re-asks the corridor.  Nothing searches for that set.

## 8. WHAT THIS ITERATION FOUND, IN ONE SENTENCE

**The wall on this board is no longer FINDING a cut — it is PUTTING THE CUT
COPPER BACK.**  Every transaction now dies at the relay, and every one of them
names exactly ONE net that will not go back: `NFC_RFO2` (twice),
`Net-(U12-PS_SYNC)`, `Net-(J3-CC2)`, `/I2S_LRCLK`+`GND`.

## 9. THE PLANE-HAUL FAMILY IS EXHAUSTED, AND ITS SIXTH CLOSURE WAS NEVER PRICED

D-635 swept **87 island pairs** with a reserved plane offered; **6 closed**;
D-636 priced four and refused all four (`RP3` for `In1`, `RP5`+`RP4` for the
two USB pairs).  The SIXTH was never examined, and it is not a plane question
at all: `/NFC_SUPPLY C55.1 <-> U9.8` closes at 0.300 mm on **`B -> I2 -> B`**,
and **`In2` is not a reserved plane** — `reserved_inner_planes` on this board
is `{I1: GND, I3: +3V3, I4: GND}` and `In2` is already inside `P3V3`'s
permitted set `('F','B','I2')`.  It is a WIDTH question, and the board's own
section-5 IPC-2221B table refuses it twice over: `P3V3` requires **0.300 mm
outer / 1.563 mm inner at the 1.0 A design current** (0.162 / 0.844 mm at the
0.64 A measured peak), and the authored floor is **0.400 mm on the outer
layers**.  A 0.300 mm run with an `In2` leg is below both.  Licensing it needs
a published per-net current for `U9`'s VDD/VDD_TX rail, which this repository
does not carry — the SAME KIND OF GAP as `/I2S_LRCLK`'s edge rate, and the
second thing D-636 item 1's per-part electrical ledger would unlock.

## 10. WHAT IS NOT SHIPPED

An `--avoid-cut-net` preference lever — try a named net's tracks LAST when
choosing which track to cut — was written in this iteration BEFORE the
measurement was taken.  The measurement says both opening lands are `SOLE_CUT`:
there is no choice to make on this board today.  **It is not shipped.**
Shipping an unexercised action lever into a promoting-adjacent screen is the
complexity the simplification doctrine names, and `screen_cut_choice` is the
instrument that would justify one the day a land reports `CHOICE`.

## NEXT, IN ORDER OF LEVERAGE

 1. **BUILD THE CUT-SET RETRY — one lever, and it is the only thing between
    this board and its next closures.**  When a relay chain fails it is the CUT
    SET that is refused, not the transaction, and `screen_corridor_detour`
    already computes the proof that a better set exists: `irreducible_nets` is
    EMPTY for `NFC_VDD_RF`, which means holding out every crossing track except
    `NFC_RFO2`'s DOES open that corridor.  Drop the failing net from the cut
    pool, re-run `minimal_tracks`, retry — the search is bounded and guaranteed
    to terminate, because a net that IS irreducible is reported as such and
    ends it.  Section 8 says every remaining transaction dies at the relay;
    this is the arm that asks the second question.
 2. **`GND J3.A12/B1` IS THE BEST CANDIDATE ON THE BOARD.**  Its sole cut is
    the only UNCITED opener here, and D-638 already ruled its relay a
    `LATTICE_WALL` — a refusal of the grid, not of the board.  It has been
    asked at 0.050 and 0.025 mm and never finer.  A `--grid 10000` joint arm is
    a bounded, cheap question with copper on the other side of it.
 3. **`Net-(U12-PS_SYNC)` IS THE WHOLE OF `BQ25185_SYS C26.2`** — two of three
    relays already succeed and the land is one net from closing, on the net
    with the most open edges on the board.
 4. **FINISH THE CORRIDOR SWEEP** — 12 nets never started, 1 timed out at
    1500 s.  `/ACC_PWR_EN` needs a coarser grid or a bounded minimal search;
    the reverse-greedy is O(crossing tracks) `route_join` calls and
    `NFC_VDD_RF` had 170 of them.
 5. **THE PER-PART ELECTRICAL LEDGER (D-636 item 1) NOW UNLOCKS TWO EDGES, NOT
    ONE**: `/I2S_LRCLK`'s edge rate for `RP4` and `/NFC_SUPPLY`'s per-net
    current for the section-9 width question.
 6. **CARRIED UNCHANGED**: PM-3 now has SEVEN lands whose escape is blocked by
    their own package's adjacent pin, each named and measured (section 4);
    `R129.1`'s absent plane remains a POUR question; D-618's `J3` question
    remains RECORDED.  No owner decision is OPEN.

D-638 closed with three ranked items and all three are now measured.

## 1. THE RUNG TRAVELS WITH THE PLAN (D-638 item 1) -- and it was worth a whole gate run

`screen_relay_transaction.py --plan-out` now emits the width the measurement
was TAKEN at, and `route_maze_batch.gate` adopts it when the caller named none:

    "rung": {"name": "floor", "stitch_width_nm": 150000,
             "stitch_via_dia_nm": 500000, "stitch_via_drill_nm": 200000,
             "argv": ["--stitch-width","150000","--stitch-via","500000:200000"]}

The gate's own child was invoked `--stitch-width 150000 --stitch-via
500000:200000` and the summary records `detour.rung.adopted: true`,
`cli_stitch_width: null`, `conflict: false`.  An explicit CLI rung still wins
and the disagreement is RECORDED rather than silently resolved; the adopted
figures still go through the same clamp UP to `BOARD_TRACK_MIN` and the
`.kicad_dru` class floors, so **a plan can license nothing**.  A plan that
closed lands at two different rungs states that instead of picking one, because
`--stitch-width` is run-wide.

The consequence is measurable on this board: given the floor rung, the `GND`
stitch pass is left with exactly **TWO** unreachable islands -- `J3.A12/B1`
(`NO_BODY_VIA_SITE`, no legal 0.50 mm barrel inside the body pour) and `MK1.4`
(`NO_LEGAL_ESCAPE at >= 0.150 mm`, blocked by its own mounting pad 67 times and
the board edge 5) -- where D-638's netclass-rung run reported four and named
none of them the same way.

## 2. A TRACK IS A SLOT IN A FOREIGN POUR EXACTLY AS A BARREL IS (D-638 item 2)

New `maze3d.copper_severs` answers `_antipad_severs`' question for ARBITRARY
new copper: a barrel is a disc on the whole stack, a track is a capsule of
`w/2 + clearance + min_thickness` on ONE layer, and an island whose own lands
end in two or more surviving pieces is SEVERED.  `_antipad_severs` is
**untouched**, so its two D-605 gate-run calibrations still hold verbatim.
`screen_relay_transaction.pour_severs` charges the WHOLE transaction -- the
stitch's stub, its run, its barrel, and every segment and barrel the RELAY laid
-- against EVERY filled pour on the board, each shape carrying its own net so a
pour is never charged for its own copper.

**IT REPRODUCES D-638's GATE REFUSAL WITHOUT SPENDING A GATE RUN.**  `+3V3

## 3. AND THE LAND THAT CLOSED NEEDED NO STITCH AT ALL

`GND C37.2` at 0.050 mm (`evidence/d639-relay-joint-c372-g50.json`) is ACCEPTED

`C37.2@59.000,61.435` is a singleton cluster in the before-ledger and a member
of the 249-pad `GND` body in the after-ledger.  `PP2` reads the same event from

This is D-631's lesson at plane scale -- *the edge that closed needed no escape
at all* -- and it says something the last eight decisions did not know: **on
this board a plane land's wall can be ONE CROSSING TRACK, and the whole cure is
to move it.**

## 4. THE GATE REFUSED THAT ONCE, FOR A CLAUSE THAT HAD NOT BEEN TOLD ABOUT DETOURS

The first full-authority run of exactly this transaction was **REFUSED**
(`evidence/d639-gate-c372-refused.json`) with `promotion_candidate: false`
while every substantive clause passed: zero attributable DRC, `inherited_ok`,
no regression, no unlicensed removal, no foreign copper, `PP1-PP4` all `ok`,
**44 -> 43**.  The single dissent was clause `changed` -- "a run must CHANGE
the board" -- which counted `--plane`, `routed`, `repaired` and `bond_nets` and
**not `detour_nets`**, so a run whose only copper is a relay reads as a no-op.
`ok_nets` twenty lines above already says the opposite in its own words: *"A
DETOURED NET LAYS COPPER TOO, so its successes join the promotion set for the
same reason the repair's and the bonds' do."*  The clause was told.

**NOTHING IS WEAKENED AND THE REASON IS NOT THIS CLAUSE.**  `detour_nets` is
non-empty only where this run's own applier removed a track by signature and
`maze3d.route_points` proved it back, so the board always differs; clause 4
(`edges_after < edges_before`) still demands the board IMPROVE, and it is
clause 4 that refused D-638's own detour run at 44 -> 44 with `all_relaid:
true`.  A run with no plane, nothing routed, nothing repaired, no bond and no
detour is still exactly the vacuous promotion `changed` was written to refuse.

## 5. AND A REFUSAL NOW NAMES ITSELF

Two full-authority gate runs -- D-638's and D-639's first -- were spent working
out WHICH clause had spoken, because `ok` is a conjunction of twelve clauses
whose EVIDENCE was reported and whose VERDICT was not, and because under
`--promote` a refusal `raise`s before `--out` is ever written.  The summary now
carries a `gate_clauses` block derived from the same locals `ok` is (so it
cannot drift from it) plus `refused_clauses`, and `gate()` writes
`<work>/gate-summary.json` BEFORE the raise.  The promoted run reports twelve
`true` and `refused_clauses: []`.

## 5. AND THE GATE REFUSED IT, TWICE, FOR TWO NAMED AND FIXABLE REASONS

`--promote` refused itself and never wrote; the authoritative sha256 is
byte-identical.  `evidence/d638-gate-r39-summary.json`:

**(a) THE SCREEN AND THE WRITER WERE GIVEN DIFFERENT RUNGS, AND THE WRITER IS
RIGHT TO REFUSE.**  The measurement is taken at `screen_segment_evict`'s
`floor` rung -- `+3V3` at **0.400 mm** track and a **0.65/0.40 mm** barrel,
`needs_licence: false` -- and the writer was invoked with no rung at all, so
`net_contract` handed `stitch_net` the **NETCLASS**: `width 0.600`,
`via_dia 0.800`, `escape_floor 0.600`.  It then reported, correctly,
`R39.1 NO_BODY_VIA_SITE: no legal 0.80 mm barrel INSIDE THIS NET'S OWN BODY
POUR`, and `U4.2/U4.5/U4.8 NO_LEGAL_ESCAPE at >= 0.600 mm` where D-637's screen
records the same lands at `>= 0.400`.  `stitched: 0`.  **The transaction was
never offered the barrel it was measured with.**  `route_maze_batch.py` already
has the lever -- `--stitch-width 400000 --stitch-via 650000:400000`, clamped UP
to the `.kicad_dru` floors -- and the plan emitter must state it, because a
screen that proves a 0.65 mm barrel and a writer that asks for an 0.80 mm one
are not measuring the same board.

**(b) THE JOINT SEARCH PRICES THE BARREL AGAINST FOREIGN POURS AND DOES NOT
PRICE THE RELAY.**  `PP2` FAILED: the 17.2 mm relay is 17 mm of `B.Cu` laid
through the `GND` `B.Cu` pour and it SPLIT it, `58 -> 59` islands, shearing off
a **21.765 mm2** fragment holding `C27.2` and `C28.2`.  `PP3` finds that
fragment still `BONDED` -- two barrels into the plane at 1.902 A each -- and
`PP2` refuses it anyway because `GND` carries no published rail current to
price a fragment with (`NET_CARRIES_NO_PUBLISHED_CURRENT`).  That clause is
D-605's own lesson -- *a through barrel is a slot in every foreign pour it
passes* -- and a DETOUR TRACK is the same scissors at a different length.
`screen_relay_transaction.py` runs `maze3d._antipad_severs` over every foreign
pour for every barrel the transaction plants, and runs nothing at all for the
track it lays.

## 2. `NO_VIA_SITE` IS A MISNAMED REFUSAL, AND NAMING IT RIGHT IS THE FIX

`stitch_pad` finds its barrel with a WAVEFRONT ON THE FIELD LATTICE,
`~field.blk[L]`, inside a window of `max_mm` cells around the escape.  So its
`NO_VIA_SITE` reads as a statement about barrels and is a statement about a
POCKET -- D-633's `LATTICE_EXACT` finding in a second place, and precisely
what D-634 built `_hop_sites` over `QBoard.via_sites` to answer instead.

**NEW `maze3d.offcentre_stitch`, `cluster_body_polys`, `in_body` (add-only).**
`stitch_pad`'s question asked with D-634's answer: the LAUNCH is `_hop_launch`
(the centre-anchored `QBoard.escape` FIRST and in its own order, then
`offcentre_escapes` -- exact, never a lattice); the BARREL is `_hop_sites`,
which floods the near layer at TRACK width from the launch on the FINE grid
and is therefore a REACHABILITY answer, then clears **every layer of the
stack** and every drilled hole through `_via_free_everywhere`; the WALK is
`qrouter.connect_role` between two anchors.  And the barrel must land in the
net's own BODY POUR -- D-608's centre-in-copper contract, computed EXACTLY on
KiCad's own filled polygons instead of on a rasterised mask.

**TWO CORRECTIONS THE MEASUREMENT FORCED, BOTH INSIDE THE NEW PRIMITIVE.**

  * **THE BODY TEST IS LAYER-EXACT WHEN THERE IS NO BARREL.**  A land already
    on the layer its body pours on takes no barrel, and its stub then carries
    copper on ONE layer only -- so a containment on some other layer bonds
    nothing.  The first run of `screen_plane_stitch.py` reported `C37.2`
    CLOSED with a `B.Cu` stub whose landing lay inside the body's **`In1.Cu`**
    polygon and inside no `B.Cu` copper at all.  Not a near miss; a false
    closure, caught by writing the test down.
  * **CLAUSE 7 INSIDE THE PRIMITIVE.**  An unconstrained option with no barrel
    is a bare stub that CONNECTS NOTHING, and the same first run counted two
    of them -- `C37.2` at 1.015 mm and `U9.16` at 0.214 mm of copper joining a
    pad to open board.  They are dropped where they are generated rather than
    reported as closures.

**NEW TRACKED `screen_plane_stitch.py`** runs arm A (`stitch_pad`, unchanged,
invoked exactly as `screen_plane_orphans.py` invokes it) and arm B
(`offcentre_stitch`, with and without the body certificate) **on the same
board, the same `Field` and the same rung**, every trial reverted.

## 3. THE RESULT: ZERO, OVER 438 ISLAND-ARM TRIALS

Nine artifacts, 29 rungs, three arms per island
(`evidence/d637-plane-stitch-{3v3,gnd}.json`, `...-3v3-ceiling.json`,
`...-barrel-sweep-{3v3,gnd}-{450,400,350}.json`):

  * **WIDTH** -- from each netclass contract down to the `.kicad_dru` floor and
    on below it to 0.150 mm and 0.100 mm, the latter UNDER the board's own
    `min_track_width`.  Every sub-floor rung is flagged `licensed: false`.
  * **THE CEILING SEARCH** -- a **16 mm** barrel window, **512** candidate
    sites, **96** site options and **12** launches per land, against the 8 mm /
    96 / 24 / 6 the ordinary run uses.
  * **THE BARREL GEOMETRY, SWEPT BELOW THE BOARD'S OWN FLOOR** -- 0.45/0.20,
    0.40/0.15 and **0.35/0.10 mm**, a geometry no standard process offers,
    against the board's `min_via_diameter` 0.50 and
    `min_through_hole_diameter` 0.20.

**ACROSS ALL OF IT, `opened_B_body` IS 1.**  That one is `U9.16` at a
**0.100 mm track** -- one third under the board's own minimum -- and it is
refused a second time, independently, by §5 below.  At every fabricable rung
the answer is **ZERO, and arm A and arm B agree**.  The barrel search was not
the wall.  D-634 item 2 is CLOSED with a measured verdict rather than carried a
fourth time.

**THE ONE THING ARM A DOES THAT ARM B REFUSES, AND IT IS A POSITIVE CONTROL
FOR D-608.**  At 0.200 mm with a 0.50 mm barrel, `stitch_pad` CLOSES `R129.1`
-- 1.117 mm of copper and a barrel at (58.100, 58.000) -- and `in_body` says
that barrel lands in NO `+3V3` body copper on any layer.  That is D-607's
promoted-and-dead stitch reproduced exactly, by two instruments side by side on
one land, for the first time.

## 4. WHY IT IS ZERO — AND IT IS NOT WHAT ANY EARLIER DECISION ASSUMED

New per-island `body_gap_mm`, KiCad's own filled polygons, distance from each
orphan land to its net's BODY copper on every layer:

    U4.2 U4.3 U4.5 U4.8     In3  0.000 mm      (and F 0.000)
    C37.2 J3.A12/B1 U9.16   In1  0.000 mm  In4 0.000 mm
    U5.2                    In3  0.055 mm
    MK1.4                   every layer 1.000 mm   (its own keep-out ring)
    R39.1                   In3  1.682 mm
    R129.1                  In3  4.525 mm

**SIX OF THE TEN ISLANDS SIT AT 0.000 mm OVER THEIR OWN NET'S PLANE, AND A
SEVENTH AT 0.055 mm.**  The plane is not far away and there is nothing to haul.
The stitch needs ONE THROUGH BARREL and the entire refusal is that **there is
no room beside the land for any barrel a board can drill** -- 0.35 mm included.

`screen_segment_evict.py` (`evidence/d637-segment-evict.json`, `--body-landing
--relay-own-layer --cap 20`) then partitions the ten exhaustively:

    NOT_A_POCKET     5   the ESCAPE is refused and there is no track to cut
                         U4.2/U4.3 (U4.4 x54), U4.5 (U4.6 x41), U4.8 (U4.9 x44),
                         U5.2 (U5.1 x56), MK1.4 (its OWN footprint x67 +
                         board_edge x5)
    SEGMENT_WALL     1   R129.1 -- cut ALL 20 foreign tracks in the pocket and
                         it is STILL NO_BODY_VIA_SITE
    SEGMENT_OPENS    4   a named cut opens the barrel -- and EVERY ONE
      but RELAY-FAIL     REGRESSES the cut net 1 -> 2 clusters and CANNOT BE
                         PUT BACK

The four that open and cannot be relaid, with the cut priced:

    R39.1        cut 2 whole `Net-(U11-TS_MR)` tracks (B)      relay NO_PATH
    C37.2        cut `/ACC_DETECT_N` 5.451 mm (B) AND
                 `Net-(U11-TS_MR)` 9.527 mm (F)                relay NO_PATH
    J3.A12/B1    cut `Net-(J3-CC2)` 5.475 mm (F)               relay NO_PATH
    U9.16        cut ONE track at r = 2.00 mm, stitch 1.727 mm,
                 REJOIN -- the track is
                 `/04_SPI_B_RADIOS_NFC/NFC_RFO2`               relay NO_PATH

`/ACC_DETECT_N` is D-323's promoted copper and `NFC_RFO2` is an NFC RF output.

## 5. THE THREE LANDS A LICENCE COULD EVEN BE WRITTEN FOR, AND WHY IT WOULD NOT HELP

`checks/leaf_land_contract.py` on both nets (`evidence/d637-leaf-lands.json`,
controls **PASS 16/16**, coverage PASS) admits **THREE** of the ten islands for
a narrow escape and refuses seven:

    R129.1      SIGNAL_LEAF   100k    <= 0.055 mA   ADMITTED
    R39.1       SIGNAL_LEAF   1M      <= 0.005 mA   ADMITTED
    U4.2/U4.3   SIGNAL_LEAF   BMI270 ASDx/ASCx, bidirectional   ADMITTED
    U4.5 U4.8   RAIL          BMI270 VDDIO_5 / VDD_8, power_in
    U5.2        RAIL          UNBOUNDED_PASSIVE (MAX98357A GAIN_SLOT)
    C37.2 J3.*  RAIL          UNBOUNDED_PASSIVE
    MK1.4 U9.16 RAIL          power_in supply ports

**All three admitted lands are in the ZERO column of §3 anyway** -- R129.1 is
the `SEGMENT_WALL`, R39.1 opens only on a cut that cannot be relaid, and
`{U4.2,U4.3}` is `NOT_A_POCKET` at 0.400 mm and `NO_VIA_SITE` below it at
every barrel down to 0.35 mm.  **So no escape-relief licence this board could
lawfully write closes a single one of these ten edges.**  And the one closure
found anywhere in the campaign, `U9.16` at 0.100 mm, is refused twice over:
by the board's own `min_track_width`, and by LL4, because `U9.16` is the
ST25R3916's `GND_DR_16` **SUPPLY PORT**.

## 6. Verdict

The plane-orphan family -- 10 islands, 23 % of the board's remaining open
edges -- is **CLOSED as a routing question**.  It is not launches (D-633's
lever moves two cells and opens nothing), not barrels (D-634's search agrees
with the lattice at every geometry down to 0.35/0.10 mm), not widths, not
layers and not planes (six of ten are already ON their plane at 0.000 mm).
**Five refuse at the LAND, one refuses with its whole pocket cut, and the
remaining four are held by copper the router can no longer put back.**

That last clause is the finding that generalises, and it is the SECOND
independent measurement of it on this board: `screen_evict_rebuild.py` already
recorded `/I2C_SDA_INT` stripped whole rebuilding from 2 open edges to **4**.
**This board has reached a rip-up-and-reroute frontier -- the remaining edges
open only by evicting copper that cannot be re-proposed at today's
congestion -- and no instrument here can take that transaction, because
eviction and re-proposal are separate steps and clause 4 correctly refuses a
net that ends worse.**

**NEXT, IN ORDER OF LEVERAGE.**

 1. **THE SIMULTANEOUS RIP-UP-AND-RELAY IS THE ONE MISSING TRANSACTION.**  Four
    of these ten lands, and `/I2C_SDA_INT` before them, fail on the SAME
    clause: a cut that opens the pocket cannot be put back BECAUSE THE CUT IS
    PUT BACK ALONE.  `route_maze_batch.py --detour-spec` already applies a cut
    and `--evict` already runs before the proposal; what does not exist is a
    relay that is re-proposed WITH the opened pocket and the new stitch in one
    search.  It is bounded, it is the first thing on this board in five
    decisions whose closure would be COPPER, and `screen_segment_evict.py`
    already emits the `--detour-spec` the transaction would take
    (`--plan-out`).
 2. **FIVE OF THE TEN ARE A PLACEMENT FINDING AND SHOULD BE RECORDED AS ONE.**
    `U4.5`, `U4.8`, `{U4.2,U4.3}`, `U5.2` and `MK1.4` are refused by their OWN
    PACKAGE NEIGHBOURS and their own footprint -- `MK1.4` by `MK1.` itself 67
    times and the board edge 5 more.  No router, width, barrel or layer
    reaches them; only moving a part or changing a footprint does.
 3. **`R129.1` IS THE ONE LAND WHOSE PLANE IS GENUINELY ABSENT.**  4.525 mm to
    the nearest `+3V3` body copper on `In3` and 5.223 mm on `F` -- it is
    outside the pour, not sealed from it -- so its question is where `In3`
    stops, which is a POUR question and not a stitch question.
 4. **THE D-636 ITEMS ARE CARRIED UNCHANGED**: the `/I2S_LRCLK` edge rate is
    still a DATA task and still the only thing between `/I2C_SCL_INT` and the
    board's first plane haul; the `GND` stitch barrels still ride with it;
    RP2/RP4 can still be aimed at the board.

No owner decision is OPEN.  D-618's `J3` question remains RECORDED and PM-3
remains an open PLACEMENT finding, now with four named lands beside it.

    authority  5715bf5cd688a87f686e162b77bbcbff98dc9f9f3e20b4be6424849423e690d2
            -> 5715bf5cd688a87f686e162b77bbcbff98dc9f9f3e20b4be6424849423e690d2
    NO COPPER MOVED.  Zero tracks, zero vias, zero zones, zero rule areas,
      zero `.kicad_dru` change, zero placement change.  Every screen re-reads
      the board's sha256 after its last trial and reports
      `authoritative_unchanged: true`.
    NO EXISTING FILE CHANGED.  `git diff --numstat` over the whole worktree is
      EMPTY: two new tracked instruments and their evidence, add-only, not one
      line of any promoting instrument touched.  The ten standing contracts
      were re-run and compared field by field anyway --
      `evidence/d636-contract-regression.json`, **10/10 ran, 10/10 IDENTICAL**.

D-635 closed with a ranked list whose first item was unambiguous: *"PRICE THE
`GND` RETURN PATH ... `PP2` is the clause and `screen_plane_slot.py` already
produces the geometry it would price.  The `GND` return-path price is now the
ONLY thing between a measured closure at full trunk width and copper."*

**It is priced.  The clause exists, it is mechanical, and it refuses all three
of the closures D-635 found — each by a DIFFERENT clause, and one of them by
the board's own authored rule rather than by a judgement call.**

## 1. The gap, and why it had stayed open since D-628

`PP2` prices a POUR severance in amperes.  It has never been able to price a
PLANE severance, and the reason is structural: a reference plane is not
carrying the current that matters.  It is carrying somebody ELSE's return
current, and the cost of cutting it is paid by traces the cut never touches.
D-628 recorded it as *"the one OPEN modelling gap in `PP2`"*; D-632, D-633,
D-634 and D-635 each carried it forward unclosed.

**New tracked `checks/plane_return_path.py`, RP1..RP6.**  Every term is
measured off the board:

  * WHICH traces pay -- the ones whose nearest reference is this plane, i.e.
    the copper layers adjacent to it in `GetEnabledLayers().CuStack()`.  Never
    transcribed: `.kicad_dru` section 2b states the intent (*"L2 (In1)
    references the F.Cu side, L5 (In4) references the B.Cu side"*) and the
    board states the fact.
  * WHICH of them pay -- the ones that CROSS.  A trace running alongside a
    slot, or ending beside it, keeps a continuous return.
  * HOW MUCH -- exactly.  The return follows the void's own boundary, so the
    detour is the shorter boundary ARC between where the trace enters the void
    and where it leaves, MINUS the chord it wanted.  Both are computed on the
    real void outline.

`RP1` plane survives, `RP2` reference inventory, `RP3` class refusal, `RP4`
detour budget, `RP5` the haul's own return, `RP6` return transfer at the
barrels.

**RP3 IS A POINTER INTO THE RULES, NEVER A SECOND COPY OF THEM.**  Each of the
seven reference-critical netclasses cites a live `.kicad_dru` rule BY ITS EXACT
NAME, and the clause FAILS if the cited rule is not present in the `.kicad_dru`
beside the board -- so retiring or renaming a rule breaks this check loudly
instead of silently widening it.  Both integrity checks are clean on the
current board: `citations_missing_from_dru: []`, `classes_absent_from_board:
[]`.

**RP4 REFUSES TO INVENT A NUMBER, WHICH IS THE D-633 LL-C DOCTRINE APPLIED
AGAIN.**  The budget is `rise_length / 20` where
`rise_length = edge_ns * c / sqrt(epsilon_r)`.  `epsilon_r` is read from the
BOARD's own stack-up -- **4.4, giving 142.920 mm/ns** -- and the WORST value is
taken, because the slowest propagation gives the shortest rise length and the
tightest budget.  `--edge-ns` has **NO DEFAULT and the clause refuses to run
without it**: this repository does not publish the edge rate of any net, and
D-633's LL-C already ruled that inventing an unpublished electrical figure is
not something a clause may do.  Stating it on the command line puts it in the
artifact, where it can be argued with.  Every run below is at
**`--edge-ns 1.0`, a deliberately conservative floor for a 3.3 V CMOS GPIO,
giving a 142.920 mm rise length and a 7.146 mm budget.**

## 2. "THE CHOICE OF PLANE IS FREE" — REFUTED

D-635 published that offering only `In4.Cu` closes the same three pairs at the
same widths as `In1.Cu` and concluded *"the choice of plane is FREE"*.  It is
free to the ROUTER.  It is decisively **not** free to the board, and the two
hauls are the SAME COPPER cutting two completely different sets of return
paths.

New tracked `screen_plane_haul.py` reproduces D-635's closure and publishes
the EXACT geometry -- every segment, layer, width and barrel, dumped from
`qb.laid` before the revert -- which `screen_offcentre_hop.py` computes and
throws away.  `/I2C_SCL_INT` `U1.38 <-> TP5.1` closes at the full 0.200 mm
netclass trunk on **`F -> In1 -> F`** and on **`F -> In4 -> F`**, both
14.4917 mm, both 2 barrels, both at (60.2, 138.0) and (52.0, 145.8)
(`evidence/d636-plane-haul-{i1,i4}.json`).

Priced (`evidence/d636-return-path-{i1,i4}.json`), the same copper on the two
planes costs:

    In1.Cu   references F.Cu + In2.Cu   9 CROSS, 6 GRAZE   RP3 FAIL
    In4.Cu   references In3.Cu + B.Cu   3 CROSS, 0 GRAZE   RP3 PASS

**`In1.Cu` IS REFUSED BY THE BOARD'S OWN RULE.**  Four of its nine crossings
are the USB high-speed pair -- `/01_POWER_TREE/USB_D_ESD_N` twice at 12.504 mm
and 7.321 mm of return detour, `/01_POWER_TREE/USB_D_ESD_P` twice at 5.948 mm
and 6.928 mm -- and the rule RP3 cites is named
**"USB 2.0 differential pair geometry (90 ohm on F.Cu over In1)"**.  The board
already NAMES `In1` as that pair's reference plane.  A slot in `In1` under it
is refused by the design's authored intent, not by an opinion formed today.
`/SD_CS_N` is over budget besides, at 11.662 mm.

`In4.Cu` crosses **nothing reference-critical at all**: `RP3 PASS`,
`refused: 0`.  Its three crossings are `/02_MCU_CORE/DISP_BL_CTL_STRAP` at
2.593 mm, `/I2S_LRCLK` at 0.090 mm (a near-tangential crossing beside a slot
end, which is what a free crossing looks like) and `/I2S_LRCLK` again at
**7.670 mm** -- against the 7.146 mm budget.

**Both planes pass RP1 identically**: outlines 1 -> 1, 8.902 mm2 lost, **268
anchors, 0 off the main body** -- and note that this is the REAL path at the
ZONE's own 0.250 mm clearance with both barrel anti-pads included, where
D-635's `screen_plane_slot.py` measured the worst-case STRAIGHT cut at the
0.200 mm netclass clearance.  The stronger question gives the same answer.

**RP6 IS THE TERM THAT MAKES THEM DIFFERENT PRICES FOR IDENTICAL COPPER.**  The
haul's outer ends are on `F.Cu`, which references `In1`.  A haul ON `In1` never
changes reference domain -- `transfer_needed: false`, nothing to charge.  A
haul on `In4` does, and the only thing that carries the return across is a
`GND` through barrel near the signal barrel: the nearest are **3.754 mm and
2.818 mm** away.  Both are inside the budget so RP6 passes, but the cost is
real, it is now measured, and the cheap mitigation -- a `GND` stitch barrel at
each signal barrel -- is named here so a future promoting transaction carries
it.

## 3. The 7.670 mm crossing is FORCED BY THE BOARD, not chosen by the router

Three independent levers, eighteen read-only trials, every one reverted
(`evidence/d636-plane-haul-levers.json`):

  1. **FIVE `--far` SETS AT TWO GRIDS.**  `F,B,I2,I4` / `F,I2,I4` / `F,B,I4` /
     `F,I4` / `F,B,I2,I1,I4`, at 100 um and 50 um.  All ten close; all ten are
     ONE path family (14.4917 mm at 100 um, 14.7661 mm at 50 um, 2 barrels
     every time) and every member crosses `/I2S_LRCLK` at the same place for
     the same 7.67-7.79 mm.
  2. **THE FRAMEWORK'S OWN `--return-keepout`** -- new to
     `screen_plane_haul.py`, and the natural next question the price itself
     asks: project the referencing layers' copper onto the plane as obstacles,
     via the same add-only idiom
     `incremental_router.inject_existing_via_obstacles` uses for barrels, so
     the search is FOR a crossing-free path.  Projecting all 1830 segments of
     `B.Cu + In3.Cu` gives `NO_PATH`.  Projecting only `/I2S_LRCLK` (12
     segments) CLOSES -- and is **strictly worse**: 29.4474 mm instead of
     14.4917, **`RP1` SEVERS**, and one crossing becomes EIGHT, including
     `Net-(J3-SHIELD)` at 19.773 mm and `/I2S_BCLK` at **23.287 mm**.
     Protecting the two crossing nets together is worse again.
  3. **`--plane-block`** -- forbid `In4` east of the crossing so the slot must
     START past it, which is the cheap answer wherever a crossing is forced,
     because the detour is twice the distance to the nearest slot END.
     `NO_PATH` at **every rung from x = 59.0 down to x = 57.0**.  The barrel at
     (60.2, 138.0) is the ONLY door out of `U1.38` into the plane.

**So the licence for this edge costs exactly one number, and the number cannot
be reduced by routing.**

## 4. The other two closures D-635 found are refused by a different clause

`/USB_D_MCU_N` `R33.2 <-> U1.13` and `/USB_D_MCU_P` `R34.2 <-> U1.14` both
close on `F -> In4 -> F` at 0.250 mm (`evidence/d636-plane-haul-USB_D_MCU_*.json`).
Both are refused by **RP5**: the HAUL'S OWN class is reference-critical, and a
USB high-speed pair routed inside a slot in a reference plane is the fault the
whole clause exists to name.  **RP4 refuses them anyway**, at 19.622 mm and
19.928 mm of induced detour on other traces.  RP5 was not a dead clause written
for symmetry; it fires on the first pair it was ever shown.

## 5. Verdict, and the ONE datum that decides the remaining edge

    /I2C_SCL_INT  U1.38<->TP5.1  on In1.Cu   REFUSED  RP3 -- the USB HS pair
                                                      crosses its own
                                                      DRU-named reference
                                                      plane four times
    /I2C_SCL_INT  U1.38<->TP5.1  on In4.Cu   PENDING  RP1/RP2/RP3/RP5/RP6 PASS.
                                                      RP4 alone, by 0.524 mm on
                                                      ONE crossing, at a
                                                      1.0 ns stated edge floor
    /USB_D_MCU_N  R33.2<->U1.13   either      REFUSED  RP5 (and RP4)
    /USB_D_MCU_P  R34.2<->U1.14   either      REFUSED  RP5 (and RP4)

The `In4` edge is not a routing wall.  It is a **DATA** gap of exactly one
figure: the output edge rate of the driver on `/I2S_LRCLK`.  At the 1.0 ns
floor stated here the budget is 7.146 mm and the measured detour is 7.670 mm --
a 7.3% overrun inside a deliberately conservative assumption.  Any published
vendor edge rate at or above 1.08 ns admits the edge outright.  **That figure
is NOT invented here**, for the same reason D-633's LL-C declined to invent the
BMI270's performance-mode current: the repository does not carry it, and a
clause may not manufacture the datum that decides it.

**NEXT, IN ORDER OF LEVERAGE.**

 1. **READ THE EDGE RATE OFF THE PARTS AND RECORD IT.**  `/I2S_LRCLK`'s driver
    and receiver are named in the schematic and their datasheets are ordinary
    vendor documents; `docs/full-beta-v2/assembly/SOURCING_LEDGER.md` already
    carries the identities D-614/D-615 ruled orderable.  A per-part
    `edge_ns` column is a small, bounded, machine-readable addition that RP4
    reads instead of a command-line argument -- and it retires the ONLY thing
    between this board and its first plane haul.  It is worth more than one
    edge: RP4 is the clause every future plane licence will be decided by.
 2. **CARRY THE `GND` STITCH BARRELS.**  If the `In4` edge is admitted, the
    promoting transaction owes a `GND` through barrel beside each signal
    barrel: RP6 measures 3.754 mm and 2.818 mm today, which passes, and a
    stitch at each barrel makes it nil and improves `GND` besides.
 3. **AIM RP2/RP4 AT THE BOARD, NOT AT ONE HAUL.**  The clause takes any
    `--seg` list, so the same instrument can now ask *"where on `In4.Cu` could
    a slot be cut for free?"* -- a map of the plane's crossing-free corridors,
    which is the thing that would tell the next iteration WHICH open edge to
    aim a plane haul at instead of re-asking the one D-635 happened to find.
 4. **THE 82 PAIRS THAT DID NOT MOVE ARE STILL A PLACEMENT PROBLEM** (PM-3),
    carried unchanged from D-635 item 2, and the **barrel-search corrections
    still belong in the promoting instruments**, carried unchanged from D-634
    item 2.

The `GND` return-path pricing question is **CLOSED as a modelling gap** and
reopened as a data task.  No owner decision is OPEN; D-618's `J3` question
remains RECORDED and PM-3 remains an open PLACEMENT finding.

## 0. First, D-634 was RECOVERED and COMMITTED — and one claim in it had never been measured

The D-634 session ended with its work uncommitted and its fourth pair-sweep
shard -- `+3V3`, `GND` and `/01_POWER_TREE/BQ25185_SYS`, the three pour-owning
nets and by far the most expensive -- **still running**, its artifact never

The shard's own process was still alive on the worker under its original
`timeout 7000` wrapper with its original arguments
(`--route --pairs 1 --max-gap-mm 40 --limit 4`), so it was allowed to finish
rather than re-run under arguments chosen after the fact; a duplicate started
under guessed flags was killed by PID before it could write.  **The artifact is
D-634's own run and not a reconstruction of it.**

The claim then verified, over all four shards, on a board whose `sha256` never
moved:

    21 open retained nets, 85 pairs
      1  CLOSED   /NFC_SUPPLY C55.1 <-> U9.8, 12.375 mm, 0.300 mm,
                  B -> In2.Cu -> B, 2 barrels, licensed_unconditionally FALSE

## 1. The via field, audited — new tracked `screen_via_field.py`

    evidence/d635-via-field-in2.json     read-only, authoritative_unchanged

Every one of the 790 barrels, classified twice.  **Attachment** is what the
barrel is tied to, read from KiCad's own track endpoints and pad hit-tests:

    LAYER_CHANGE   460   track endpoints on two or more distinct layers
    TERMINAL_DROP  324   exactly one layer of track; the far end is a pour,
                         a plane, or nothing
    PAD_ONLY         2
    FREE_STITCH      4   no track, no land -- the ONLY barrels on this board
                         that carry no copper of their own

**FOUR.**  The hypothesis that a large share of the field is retirable pour
stitching has, on this board, exactly four candidates.  Of the 250 `GND`
barrels, 247 are terminal drops carrying a track to a plane and retiring one
orphans a land.

**Which layers a barrel SERVES, as against which it merely TRANSITS**, is the
classification that matters, and it is read the same way -- a track endpoint, a
same-net land, or a same-net FILLED ZONE polygon (`GetFilledPolysList`)
containing the barrel's centre.  Against `In2.Cu`, the one inner layer the
stack-up does not give to a plane:

    SERVES_In2     222   the net has copper on In2.Cu at this barrel
    TRANSITS_In2   524   the served span STRADDLES In2.Cu and serves nothing
                         there -- a pure obstacle on the only spare layer
    AVOIDS_In2      44   the span lies entirely on one side of In2.Cu, so the
                         barrel crosses it for no reason at all

All 250 `GND` and all 73 `+3V3` barrels are `TRANSITS_In2`.

## 2. And it buys almost nothing — the counterfactual arms

Same screen, same measurement D-634 published (`QBoard.grid` at 0.200 mm width
and clearance on a 0.150 mm lattice, then 8-connected components of the free
cells), re-run with named SUBSETS of the barrel field withheld.  Withholding is
exact and needs no scratch board: `qrouter._scan` skips `PCB_VIA` and injection
is what makes a barrel visible, so an arm is a fresh `QBoard` with only its own
subset injected.

    arm          barrels  In2.Cu free   pieces   largest piece
    asbuilt          790    6524.6 mm2     223   3425.5 mm2  52.5%   <- CONTROL
    no_avoid         746    6572.2         207   3443.2      52.4%
    no_transit       222    7207.9         108   4043.6      56.1%
    no_vias            0    7272.3          94   4078.2      56.1%

The control reproduces D-634's published `In2.Cu` row field for field, which is
the only reason the other three mean anything.

**DELETING THE ENTIRE VIA FIELD -- all 790 barrels, the absolute physical
ceiling that no technology and no design change can beat -- MOVES `In2.Cu`'s
LARGEST CONNECTED PIECE FROM 52.5% TO 56.1% OF ITS FREE AREA.**  The arm that
is buildable today, blind or buried barrels for the 44 that cross `In2.Cu` for
no reason, moves it from 52.5% to 52.4%.

**So D-634's item 1 and item 4 are both CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT.**  No via
campaign -- retirement, relocation, or a blind/buried stack-up -- changes what
`In2.Cu` can carry.  The owner decision D-634 recorded on blind and buried
vias is now priced, and the price is 3.6 percentage points of largest-piece
share at the theoretical limit.

**AND WHAT DOES PARTITION IT IS NAMED.**  With every barrel withheld, `In2.Cu`
still carries **422 obstacles: 305 foreign track segments totalling 2403.9 mm
of copper, and 56 through-hole lands.**  `In2.Cu` is not a spare lane that the
vias ruined.  It is a working signal layer that is already full, and D-634 read
its own measurement the wrong way round.

## 4. What offering a plane actually buys — new tracked `checks/pair_sweep_diff.py`

    evidence/d635-plane-pairs-{A,B,C,D}.json        read-only
    evidence/d635-plane-pairs-in4-only.json         read-only

D-634's own pair sweep, re-run with **one thing changed** -- `--far` gains
`I1,I4` -- and diffed pair by pair.  The diff is a tracked driver now and not a

Over ALL 21 open retained nets -- the same net set, the same 85 pairs, the
same widths, the same barrels -- **GAINED 3, LOST 0, SAME 82.**

    /I2C_SCL_INT   U1.38 <-> TP5.1   13.286 mm   NO_PATH -> CLOSES at the FULL
                   0.200 mm netclass trunk, 2 barrels, F -> In1.Cu -> F,

    /USB_D_MCU_N   R33.2 <-> U1.13   21.858 mm   NO_PATH -> 0.250 mm, F->In1->F

`/I2C_SCL_INT` is the largest open net on this board and D-629 recorded fifteen
of its pairs as `NO_PATH` with a legal escape at both ends of every one.  One

**AND THE CHOICE OF PLANE IS FREE.**  Re-run offering only `In4.Cu`, all three
close on `F -> In4.Cu -> F` at the same widths.  Whichever plane's reference
duty is lighter under the corridor is the one the licence may name.

**AND EIGHTY-TWO OF EIGHTY-FIVE DO NOT MOVE.**  The plane is capacity, and the
wall is not only capacity: what is left refuses as `NO_LEGAL_ESCAPE` on lands
this board has already enumerated, or as `NO_PATH` in a local pocket a fresh
layer 0.1 mm away does not reach.

## 5. What it costs — new tracked `screen_plane_slot.py`

    evidence/d635-plane-slot-{i2c,usb,usb-in4,all}.json   read-only

A signal track on a plane is a SLOT.  KiCad re-pours around it exactly as D-584
measured on the outer pours, so the first half of the licence question is
geometric and answerable now: does the plane stay one piece, and does every
barrel bonded to it stay bonded?  The plane's own filled polygon set, minus the
proposed run stroked at `width/2 + clearance` with a disc at each end; then
every same-net barrel and land is re-located by outline.

    cut                          outlines   area mm2            anchors off body
    /I2C_SCL_INT alone, In1        1 -> 1   9429.5 -> 9423.8    0 of 268  SURVIVES
    USB pair alone, In1            1 -> 3   9429.5 -> 9411.0    1 of 268  SEVERS
    USB pair alone, In4            1 -> 3   9429.5 -> 9411.0    1 of 268  SEVERS
    all three together, In1        1 -> 3   9429.5 -> 9405.6    1 of 268  SEVERS

The barrel that leaves the main body is `U1.41`, an MCU `GND` land, and it
leaves it for both planes identically -- the straight line between the USB
pair's two chosen barrel sites runs through the MCU's own ground land.  The cut
is the WORST-CASE straight segment between those sites and not the path the
router found, so `SEVERS` there is a warning about where those endpoints sit
rather than a verdict on a routed haul.  **`SURVIVES` for `/I2C_SCL_INT` is the
stronger claim, because it holds at the worst case**: one outline before and
after, 5.7 mm2 lost out of 9429.5, and all 268 anchors still on the main body.

**The USB pair is refused here on an independent ground and the geometry is
beside the point.**  `USB_D_MCU_P` / `USB_D_MCU_N` are the one differential
pair on this board whose signal integrity depends on an unbroken reference
plane.  Slotting the plane they reference is not a question this screen is
entitled to answer with an area figure.

## 6. So the licence candidate is exactly ONE edge, and what blocks it is a MODEL

`/I2C_SCL_INT` `U1.38 <-> TP5.1`: 13.286 mm, the FULL 0.200 mm netclass trunk,
no width licence of any kind, on either GND plane, and the plane survives the
worst-case cut with 0.06% of its area lost and nothing orphaned.

It is not promoted, and the reason is doctrine this board has already written
down.  `route_maze_batch.reserved_inner_planes` reserves `In1.Cu` and `In4.Cu`
to `GND`, and no `.kicad_dru` rule area names a corridor in either.  Authoring
that licence before the return path is priced would be exactly the unpriced
severance D-627 refused and D-628 accepted only once the bond it cut had been
measured at 1.441 A against a published 1.0 A rail.  **The GND return-path
price is the one open modelling gap in `PP2`, and it has just become the only
thing standing between a measured closure at full trunk width and copper.**

## 7. Next, in order of leverage

  1. **PRICE THE GND RETURN PATH.**  It was a modelling gap with no consumer;
     it now has one, and the consumer is a full-width closure on the largest
     open net on the board.  The question is bounded: for a slot of a given
     length and position in `In1.Cu` or `In4.Cu`, which `F.Cu` / `B.Cu` runs
     cross it, how far must their return current detour, and what does that
     cost at the frequencies those nets actually carry.  `PP2` is the clause
     it belongs in and `screen_plane_slot.py` already produces the geometry it
     would price.
  2. **THE EIGHTY-TWO THAT DID NOT MOVE ARE NOT A LAYER PROBLEM.**  A fresh
     8635 mm2 connected surface changed three refusals out of eighty-five.
     The rest are pad pockets and local congestion, and the only lever this
     board has left for those is PLACEMENT -- PM-3 remains the open placement
     finding.
  3. **THE BARREL-SEARCH CORRECTIONS STILL BELONG IN THE INSTRUMENTS THAT
     PROMOTE** -- `_via_free_everywhere` and `via_sites(separation=dia)`,
     carried unchanged from D-634 item 2, and still owing their own no-op
     control because `relief_stitch` / `stitch_pad` / `bridge_islands` promote.
  4. **D-634 ITEM 1 AND ITEM 4 ARE CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT** and are recorded
     here as closed so that no future iteration re-opens them: the via field
     is not retirable (four free stitches on the whole board) and blind or
     buried barrels are worth 3.6 percentage points of `In2.Cu` largest-piece
     share at the theoretical ceiling, which is not a fab cost worth paying.

No owner decision is OPEN.  D-618's `J3` question remains RECORDED, PM-3
remains an open PLACEMENT finding, and the blind/buried stack-up question
D-634 RECORDED is now answered against on evidence rather than left standing.

    authority  5715bf5cd688a87f686e162b77bbcbff98dc9f9f3e20b4be6424849423e690d2
            -> 5715bf5cd688a87f686e162b77bbcbff98dc9f9f3e20b4be6424849423e690d2

      zero `.kicad_dru` change, zero placement change.  Every screen re-reads
      the board's sha256 after its last trial and reports
      `authoritative_unchanged: true`.
    retained open edges  44 (unchanged)   open retained nets 21
      connected retained 152   raw ratsnest 60
    FRAMEWORK + CHARACTERISATION.  D-633 ranked an OFF-CENTRE HOP first "in
      order of leverage" -- "the exact stub, a barrel at the first via site the
